name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 Honolulu-area district with incumbent Ed Case seeking re-election
Republican Adriel Lam shows no reported fundraising or outside support against Case's $1.3 million raised
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent
No public general-election polling or expert ratings exist for the race
model.rationale: Case is an entrenched incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 13 points, holding a large financial advantage over a challenger with no visible fundraising, and markets price the race near certainty. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the evidence points to a comfortable Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or unexpected polling showing a much tighter race would be the first sign the margin, though unlikely the outcome, could narrow.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st District covers urban Honolulu and leans strongly Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 13 points. Ed Case, who has held the seat since 2019 after earlier service in Congress, is seeking another term and has raised roughly $1.3 million with $450,000 on hand. His Republican opponent, Adriel Lam, shows no reported fundraising, while Green and independent candidates add minor names to the ballot.

No public general-election polls or independent race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, Case's incumbency, and the wide spending gap. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent. Recent cycles in this seat have produced double-digit Democratic margins, and nothing in the current evidence suggests competitiveness; the open question is the size of Case's winning margin rather than the winner.
